'''Shitomi Shrine''' (志等美神社) is a shrine in Japan associated with the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|lt=Kōtai Jingū|lt=Outer Shrine|ja|外宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Outer Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 豊受大神宮}} of the {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine}}. This article also covers the {{ill|Shitomi Shrine|lt=Shitomi Shrine|lt=Ōkōchi Shrine|ja|大河内神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkōchi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 志等美神社}}, which shares the same grounds as Shitomi Shrine, as well as the {{ill|Shitomi Shrine|lt=Shitomi Shrine|lt=Uchikake Shrine|ja|打懸神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uchikake Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 志等美神社}} and the former village shrine known as {{ill|Shitomi Shrine|lt=Shitomi Shrine|lt=Kami Shrine (Ise)|ja|上社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kami Shrine (Ise)}}, which encompasses all three shrines within its precincts.

Among the 125 shrines affiliated with Ise Grand Shrine, only Shitomi, Ōkōchi, and Uchikake shrines hold recognized Ranks in the {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|en|Shinkai (divine rank)|qid=Q11591025|lt=Shinto shrine Ranking system}}.<ref name="sk25">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp. 342, 355.</ref>

== Overview ==

Shitomi Shrine is located at Tsuji Kuru 1-13, Ise City, Mie Prefecture. The precincts are under the jurisdiction of Kami Shrine, with Shitomi, Ōkōchi, and Uchikake shrines positioned at the right side of Kami Shrine's eastern entrance.<ref name="uy9">Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): Vol. 2, p. 949.</ref> The total area of the precincts is approximately 700 tsubo (about 2,314 square meters), of which 406 square meters are occupied by Shitomi, Ōkōchi, and Uchikake shrines.<ref name="sk36">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp. 343, 356.</ref> Shitomi and Ōkōchi shrines share the same fence, facing south, and feature {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|en|Shinmei-zukuri|qid=Q930545|lt=Shinmei-zukuri}} architecture with wooden plank roofs.<ref name="sk36"/> These shrines do not have offering boxes.

== Shitomi Shrine ==

Shitomi Shrine Ranks 7th among the 16 auxiliary shrines of the Outer Shrine.<ref name="uy">Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): Vol. 1, pp. 7, 11–12.</ref> Historical records also refer to it as "Shitomi-no-Iba Shrine," with "Shitomi-no-Iba" being the name of the surrounding wilderness.<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka Sha (2008): p. 53.</ref> Some scholars interpret "Shitomi" as derived from the verb "shitomu," meaning "to soak in water" or "to get wet." <ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 336.</ref>

== Ōkōchi Shrine ==

Although its structure is separate, Ōkōchi Shrine is located within the same fence as Shitomi Shrine.<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka Sha (2008): p. 54.</ref> It Ranks 8th among the 16 auxiliary shrines of the Outer Shrine.<ref name="uy"/> During the {{ill|Sengoku Period (Japan)|ja|戦国時代|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q117415390}}, Ōkōchi Shrine fell into disrepair and later became a component of Kami Shrine as the "Mountain Shrine."<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): Vol. 2, p. 950.</ref>

The current pronunciation of the shrine's name is "Ōkōchi," but historical documents record readings such as "Ōkahachi" and "Ōgafuchi."<ref name="sk4">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 354.</ref>

== Uchikake Shrine ==

Uchikake Shrine Ranks 4th among the eight subsidiary shrines of the Outer Shrine.<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): Vol. 1, pp. 13–15.</ref> After falling into disrepair during the Sengoku period, it was absorbed into Kami Shrine as "Parallel Shrine" (formerly "Hachioji Shrine"), maintaining its original deity.<ref name="uy8">Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): Vol. 2, p. 948.</ref>

Kami Shrine is the local {{ill|Ujigami|en|Ujigami|qid=Q767655|lt=ujigami}}, serving the districts of Nakajima, Tsuji Kuru, Futamata, and Uraguchi.<ref name="ic" /> Its treasures include a lion head for {{ill|Lion dance|en|Lion dance|qid=Q713866|lt=shishimai}} performances and a sword donated in 1721.<ref name="uy5">Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): Vol. 2, p. 955.</ref>

The precincts feature additional shrines such as Inari Shrine, Uegami Shrine dedicated to Sugawara no Michizane, and Kushitama Shrine enshrining Isetsuhiko and Isetsuhime deities, as well as remote {{ill|Haisho|ja|拝所|lt=worship sites|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haisho}} for other shrines.<ref>Ise-Shima Kirari 1000 (2013).</ref>

=== Merged Shrines ===

Kami Shrine absorbed 13 other shrines in 1909.<ref name="uyy">Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): Vol. 2, pp. 949.</ref>

== Worship and Festivals ==

Shitomi Shrine conducts annual festivals, including the {{ill|Kinensai|en|Kinen-sai|qid=Q118906710|lt=Kinensai}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinamisai|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri}}, {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|en|Kannamesai Festival|qid=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai Festival}}, and {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|en|Niiname-no-Matsuri|qid=Q11501518|lt=Niinamesai}}.<ref name="sk343,355">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp. 343, 355.</ref>

Kami Shrine's events include the {{ill|Mitō-shinji|ja|御頭神事|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mitō-shinji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} on January 15 and its annual festival on July 15.<ref name="uy5"/>
